description: Workload requirements and ownership notes for CPU-only scientific stages. This document is not a CPU stage class map: it states what the classes must satisfy and who owns each queue, while the classes themselves are assembled by modules/kueue-scheduling and validated against the shape named in 'describes' (catalog/runtime/schema/cpu-stage-classes.schema.json). Giving it the class schema ID would claim it validates as one. Canonical CPU stage classes for scientific batch placement. This file is the coordination record, not a second contract. The scheduling workstream is the sole producer of the reference-data class, the sole assembler of the scheduling contract, and the sole owner of the immutable content-addressed ConfigMap that publishes it. The general CPU lane contributes exactly one canonical general-cpu entry plus the ownership facts for the queues it creates, and publishes no document, ConfigMap or digest of its own.

entry_producers.reference-data: scheduling workstream, from the infrastructure reference-data storage contract
entry_producers.general-cpu: modules/general-cpu-scheduling, from deployment.cpu_pools and the one general lane configuration

contract_fields.cpu_classes_schema: the versioned schema of the class entries
contract_fields.cpu_class_digests: per-class digest of each contributed entry, so a producer can prove the assembled contract carries the exact revision it rendered

rules: Exactly one Terraform owner assembles the classes and publishes the one ConfigMap the controller consumes.
A producer contributes only its own class; it never merges, adapts or restates another owner's class.
No producer publishes a parallel ConfigMap identity, key or digest.

Each Kueue object has exactly one owner: the general lane owns the general-cpu ResourceFlavor, ClusterQueue and LocalQueue; the reference-data plane owns its own. External lane facts describe an owner's objects without transferring ownership.
Class facts are derived, never restated: no manual cpu_stage_class_facts or operator-supplied class map exists on either side of the seam.

notes.resource_flavor: The Kueue ResourceFlavor the class admits through. Its node selector pins exactly one pool, so the flavor Kueue reports is itself the pool identity.
notes.pool_resolution: An object, and the only place the actual pool appears. {mode: per-pool-flavor, pool_id: <one of this class's eligible pools>} means the class's flavor selector pins exactly one pool, so the admitted flavor answers which node group ran the stage. {mode: node-label-observation, node_label_key: <label>} means the consumer must read that label from the scheduled Node and persist it. A class never claims Kueue binds a pool when its flavor spans several. There is no top-level pool_id.
notes.eligible_pool_ids: Scheduling is authoritative about which pools may run the class. A consumer enforces this list and never widens placement from whatever a runtime reports as compatible.
notes.schedulable_capacity: Per node, not the lane aggregate: one stage Pod must fit one node. Carries cpu, memory and ephemeral_storage as Kubernetes quantities the controller persists, alongside the raw measured numbers.

consumer_contract.verification: The controller hashes the raw bytes it mounted from the ConfigMap and compares them with the digest injected by Terraform before it enables writes. A mismatch, a missing producer or an absent class is a refusal, never a fallback.
persistence: Resolve and persist the actual resource_flavor, pool_id and cpu/memory/ephemeral_storage quantities on the admission record; do not merely parse the class.
Keep QuotaReserved and Admitted as separate states with separate timestamps; a reserved quota is not an admission.
Enforce the class's eligible_pool_ids when placing a stage, in addition to any runtime compatibility the model itself reports.
rules: An unknown class, a class with no eligible pool, or a digest mismatch is a refusal to admit, never a substitution.
general-cpu never resolves to the reference-data flavor and reference-data never resolves to a general pool, in either direction, regardless of free capacity.
A class carries the complete node selector and toleration set a Job needs; a consumer never reconstructs placement from a pool name.
consumer_contract.enablement: A reference to the scheduling ConfigMap is not proof. The assembler enables the injected seam only when the assembled cpu_classes contains a class ID and cpu_class_digests echoes the exact digest its producer rendered; otherwise the seam stays disabled and writes stay off.

general-cpu.purpose: Elastic general-purpose scientific preprocessing and aggregation that does not need the dedicated reference-data nodes.

bound_workloads.rationale: BindCraft aggregation reduces per-shard GPU design output into one ranked result set. It is CPU and memory bound, reads only artifact-store objects, and must not occupy an accelerator node or the reference-data pool.
The PyRosetta-free comparison lane aggregates identically and shares the class.

forbidden: any stage that requires the reference-data filesystem mount

reference-data.purpose: Dedicated storage-attached preprocessing on the tainted reference-data pool.

bound_workloads.rationale: The AlphaFold 3 data pipeline runs jackhmmer and nhmmer directly against the mounted reference databases. It must run on the pool that carries the reference-data filesystem, and its capacity requirement is model-requirements.json models.alphafold3.preprocessing_capacity.
Bulk database download, decompression and hashing on the same storage-attached pool.

forbidden: workloads that do not read the mounted reference databases

quota.rationale: The general CPU lane deliberately joins no cohort. Cohort membership would let general aggregation borrow reference-database capacity, or lend its own to accelerator work, and neither is intended.
quota.nominal_source: sum over eligible pools of measured per-node schedulable_capacity multiplied by that pool's maximum node count

derivation.rule: Every general-cpu fact is derived from deployment.cpu_pools and the single general lane configuration. There is no manual facts facade and no operator-supplied class map: a duplicated capacity or quota input could diverge from the pool it describes, and the divergence would only surface as a Job that never schedules.

sources.pool_id, eligible_pool_ids, node_selecto: deployment.cpu_pools plus the infrastructure general-CPU pool contract

derivation.root_preflight: The root checks every bound workload against the largest declared general CPU node before any node group is created, so an undersized pool is a plan-time answer rather than a pending BindCraft Job.

version_limits.single_execution_namespace: v1 binds one class to one namespace. The assembled contract maps a class to one LocalQueue by bare name and the controller freezes every stage of a run into one namespace, so a second namespace could not be resolved or frozen.
version_limits.single_pool_per_class: v1 binds one class to one pool, so the admitted ResourceFlavor identifies the actual node group. A heterogeneous lane needs namespace- and pool-qualified class identities across Terraform and the controller first.

global_core_admission.problem: Kueue's manager configuration excludes cpu, memory and ephemeral-storage from admission by default. A ClusterQueue that declares cpu or memory quota while they are excluded is silently inert: the quota is filtered out and admission ignores it.
global_core_admission.requirement: A general CPU pool requires global core budgeting, which the facade derives and the foundation applies. Turning it on makes core resources part of every ClusterQueue's arithmetic, so every accelerator ClusterQueue must then declare truthful cpu/memory capacity in the same combined contract.
global_core_admission.fail_closed: The workloads plan refuses before any infrastructure mutation when core budgeting is required but an accelerator ClusterQueue would be left without core capacity.
